title: Ensemble machine learning prioritized a candidate pathway tested in mouse and cell models of intestinal injury
summary: Ensemble machine-learning analysis prioritized candidate genes for follow-up in mouse and cell models of intestinal ischemia–reperfusion injury. Experimental findings support a candidate protective pathway, but datasets were small and the mechanism needs independent validation; no clinical efficacy is established.
ai_technology: Ensemble machine-learning analysis prioritized candidate genes and a pathway from transcriptomic datasets for experimental investigation.
organization: Institute (College) of Integrative Medicine, Dalian Medical University, Dalian, China

evidence.tested: Mouse and cell models provided experimental follow-up of machine-learning-prioritized candidates; the paper notes small datasets and need for independent validation.
evidence.unknown: Preclinical results do not establish human efficacy; pathway claims require independent validation.
evidence.ai_role: Ensemble machine-learning analysis prioritized candidate genes and a pathway from transcriptomic datasets for experimental investigation.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text review as recorded in case evidence; record-level claim and attribution review.
